references.text: The same threat of diseases as punishment for disobedience to the covenant, including consumption and fever that will consume the eyes and make the soul sick.
Continuation of the list of diseases with which the Lord will strike Israel as punishment for disobedience, includes boils, tumors, and scabies.
Further diseases are mentioned as part of the covenant's curses: evil sores on knees and thighs that cannot be healed.
Amos mentions blight and mildew as God's punishment upon Israel, the same agricultural disasters mentioned in Deuteronomy.
Haggai refers to blight, mildew, and hail as punishment from the Lord, the same type of curses found in Deuteronomy.
Solomon's prayer at the temple dedication mentions drought, blight, and mildew as possible punishments, with reference to the Mosaic Law.
Parallel text to 1 Kings, where Solomon asks for forgiveness when pestilence, blight, or mildew strikes the land.
